Validate vault graph facts and configured frontmatter rules

Validate vault graph facts and configured frontmatter rules.

Validation reuses graph/index facts to surface unresolved links, ambiguous links, document diagnostics, and configured frontmatter requirements. Validate does not mutate files.

USAGE
    norn validate [OPTIONS]

OPTIONS
        --format <FORMAT>
        Stdout format
        Possible values: records, jsonl, json, paths

        --summary
        Emit grouped validation finding counts instead of raw findings
        Possible values: true, false

TRIAGE FILTERS
        --code <CODE>
        Filter findings by code. Comma-separated values match any listed code

        --severity <SEVERITY>
        Filter findings by severity

        --field <FIELD>
        Filter findings by frontmatter field

        --rule <RULE>
        Filter findings by validate rule name

        --path <PATH>
        Filter findings by vault-relative path glob using config glob semantics

        --target <TARGET>
        Filter link findings by link target

        --reason <REASON>
        Filter link findings by unresolved reason

EXAMPLES
    norn validate
        # human-readable findings on the configured vault

    norn validate --format json
        # machine-readable findings for pipelines

    norn validate --severity error
        # errors only; skip warnings

    norn validate --code 'link-*'
        # broken + ambiguous links

    norn validate --code 'link-*' --format paths
        # unique source paths only; pipe-friendly

HOW VALIDATION WORKS
    Validate reads `.norn/config.yaml` for the rules that shape your vault: required frontmatter fields, allowed values, expected types, and path scoping. Each rule produces findings with a stable code and a severity (`error`, `warning`, `info`).

    Findings cover three surfaces. Frontmatter findings come from schema rules — codes like `frontmatter-required-field-missing` and `value-not-allowed`. Link findings come from graph facts — `link-target-missing`, `link-anchor-missing`, `link-block-missing`, and `link-ambiguous`. Document diagnostics come from parse — malformed frontmatter, encoding issues. Validate never writes files.

    Exit code is `1` when any finding has severity `error`, `0` otherwise. Pipelines gate on this exit code.

    Triage filters combine with AND across types and OR within a type. `--severity error --code frontmatter-required-field-missing` returns errors that match that code. `--code 'link-*'` returns the whole family. `--path 'notes/**'` scopes to a path glob; `--field`, `--rule`, `--target`, and `--reason` narrow further.

FINDING CODES
    Codes identify validation findings. Filter with --code <code>. Glob patterns supported (--code 'link-*').

    link-target-missing         A wikilink target doesn't exist in the vault.
    link-anchor-missing         The target exists but the #anchor isn't present.
    link-block-missing          The target exists but the ^block-ref isn't present.
    link-ambiguous              A wikilink resolves to multiple candidates.
    frontmatter-required-field-missing
                                A required frontmatter field is absent.
    value-not-allowed           A field's value is not in the configured set.
    field-type-invalid          A field's value doesn't match its declared type.
    frontmatter-exceeds-max-length
                                A string/list_of_strings field matches its type but exceeds max_length.
    frontmatter-forbidden-field A field that the rule forbids is present.
    document-misrouted          A doc is in a directory the rule's path selector excludes.
    frontmatter-reference-type  A field's wikilink resolves to a document whose type is outside the allowed set.

GLOBAL OPTIONS
    -C, --cwd <CWD>         Run as if norn started in this directory (default: $NORN_ROOT, else the current directory)
        --verbose           Include full diagnostic detail in output
        --no-cache-refresh  Skip the implicit cache refresh before reading the graph
        --color <COLOR>     Color output. Honors NO_COLOR / CLICOLOR_FORCE.
        --vault <NAME>      Target the registered vault with this name (see `norn vault register`)

Documentation: https://github.com/dbtlr/norn
